pairs.evidence: crates/render/src/lib.rs:5 The crate is a pure JSON-to-Markdown layer with no engine dependency, and a search of crates/render (src and tests) for compaction, max_tokens, cache_control, interpolat and context_window found nothing. It assembles no model prompt; its one prompt-related output is a verbatim, fence-safe dump of stored registry content (prompts.rs:38) for a human or an MCP caller.

techniques.evidence: crates/render/src/prompts.rs:38 This shows stored prompt text. It does not compose a prompt for a model call.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/responder/src/enrich.rs:61 The enrichment feeder stops at 10 failure lines (12 for scores) and adds no notice of what it dropped, so the investigator reads a partial view as if it were complete. The error_prompt/quality_prompt assemblers also turn missing numbers into confident zeros.

techniques.evidence: crates/responder/src/investigate.rs:37 There is one assembler function per prompt family (error_prompt, quality_prompt, build_fix_prompt), each taking typed inputs. The pipeline passes the result straight to investigate and appends nothing (pipeline.rs:146).

crates/responder/src/investigate.rs:40 A missing count renders as 'Spike: 0 failed call(s)'. Likewise, a missing drop_pct or baseline renders as '~0%' and '0.00' (line 70ff). These are fabricated values, not declared defaults or an omitted section. The hint and verify inputs do use honest '(none configured)' defaults.

crates/responder/src/enrich.rs:61 The feeder cap is silent: no '…N more not shown' line reaches the prompt. The fenced spike error string and each event's error have no length cap at all, and the prompt has no overall budget.

crates/responder/src/investigate.rs:59 Locate is present (line 46: repo is the cwd, plus an area hint), and Done is a section list. There is no Check step, such as 'open each cited file:line and confirm it before reporting'. The section list is an enumeration, which a model can satisfy by shape alone. The opening line (45) states the situation, not an expertise claim.
